subject: Performance SLOs & Autoscale: FastPay discovery follow-up
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@fastpay.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 05 Feb 2026 15:10:00 -0800
Subject: Performance SLOs & Autoscale: FastPay discovery follow-up

Hi Samir — great to meet earlier. Quick recap from today's discovery and a few follow-ups so we can scope a concise PoC and narrow sizing for Dedicated/Reserved capacity. I pulled what we discussed into bullets below and attached an editable SLO worksheet for your team.

Summary of requirements from call:
- Target SLOs: p95 latency for single-turn text generation; want to understand typical p50/p95 numbers and tail behavior.
- Streaming: first-token latency matters for chat; would like sub-200ms first-token for interactive flows if possible.
- Concurrency & throughput: typical steady-state concurrency ~200-300 reqs, but you expect bursts up to ~2000 concurrent requests during peak payroll cycles.
- Autoscale & burst: need clarification on acceptable scale-up times, warm-pool sizing, and queueing behavior during scale events.
- Fallbacks: willing to consider a slightly smaller model variant for graceful degradation if cost/latency tradeoffs are needed.

Open questions for you (so we can size and propose config):
1) Confirm target p95 numbers for our baseline: is 500ms acceptable or do you need 350-400ms?
2) For streaming chat, is the 200ms first-token requirement mandatory for all flows or just priority/agent-assisted sessions?
3) During burst windows, how long can requests queue before users perceive degradation (max tolerated queuing time)?
4) Are there regulatory/data residency constraints for any regions we should be aware of?

Proposed immediate next steps:
- You review the attached SLO worksheet and add any missing traffic/latency samples.
- We run a quick controlled perf test in our PoC infra to validate scale-up behavior and warm-pool sizing.
- Redwood to send a proposed autoscale configuration and cost estimate for both Dedicated and Hosted+Burst options.

Attachment: slo-worksheet.xlsx (editable)

Thanks — I'll follow up with a proposed config once you confirm the quick questions above.

Best,

Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

From: Samir Patel <samir@fastpay.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 06 Feb 2026 09:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Performance SLOs & Autoscale: FastPay discovery follow-up

Thanks Marissa — good notes and appreciate the worksheet. A few clarifications from our side: 

- p95 target: we'd like p95 <= 450ms for single-turn text generation under typical payloads (prompt ~250 tokens). p50 ideally < 150ms.
- Streaming: real-time chat is critical for our customer support flow. We need first-token <= 200ms for conversations classified as "live agent" priority; other flows can tolerate 300-400ms.
- Typical concurrency: steady-state 200-300. Peak bursts: up to 2000 concurrent across regions, usually for ~10-20 minutes during scheduled events. These bursts are predictable but high intensity.
- Queueing tolerance: our product team said users notice degradation after ~5 seconds of wait; anything above 3s starts to increase abandonment.
- Warm pool expectations: want warm-pool capacity that can cover the first 500 concurrent requests immediately, and then scale to full burst within ~60s. Warm pool should prefer smaller, pre-warmed workers rather than cold start.

Can you include an option that uses a prioritized warm pool + quick burst (30-60s) and an alternative that "queues + throttles" with a short tail to stay within cost targets? Also include fallback to a lower-precision quantized model for non-priority requests.

If you could send a proposed config and a rough monthly cost delta for Dedicated vs Hosted+Burst by EOD Monday that would help our procurement SOW discussion.

Samir
Head of Platform Engineering
FastPay
samir@fastpay.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@fastpay.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 08 Feb 2026 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Performance SLOs & Autoscale: FastPay discovery follow-up

Thanks — this is very helpful and gives us concrete targets. Below is a concise proposed approach we'll include in the formal PoC config (attached as slo-proposal.pdf and perf-plan.xlsx):

Autoscale & warm-pool proposal (summary):
- Baseline: provision Dedicated pool to meet steady-state concurrency 300 with headroom (suggest 400 reserved concurrency).
- Warm pool: maintain a warm-pool of ~500 pre-warmed slots (worker process context + KV cache warmed) prioritized for "live agent" traffic. Warm-pool fill maintained during predictable events per your schedule.
- Burst behavior: allow autoscaling to expand capacity to handle 2000 concurrent within 45-60s. We expect ~30-45s to add additional inference workers and another 10-15s to reach effective service throughput depending on model size.
- Queueing policy: for non-priority flows, allow short queueing window up to 3 seconds before we apply backpressure or route to quantized fallback. For priority flows, preserve sub-200ms first-token by routing to warm-pool or reserved capacity.
- Fallbacks: quantized/variant model for non-priority traffic; automatic fallback to smaller model when average latency increases above SLO thresholds.

Testing & validation plan:
1) Baseline perf run with representative prompts (we'll coordinate a 2-hour window).
2) Synthetic burst tests to validate scale-up time and queueing behavior (target: demonstrate scale to 2000 concurrent within 60s).
3) Streaming latency test for first-token SLAs (measure 95th percentile across sessions).

Next steps and timelines:
- I'll share a costed config (Dedicated vs Hosted+Burst) and a recommended autoscale policy by EOD Monday.
- Rafael, Vivek: can you please review the perf-plan attachment and add any operational constraints we should include (e.g., max GPU memory per worker, quantization profiles)?
- Samir: once you confirm the 3s queueing tolerance and the priority classification approach, we'll schedule the perf run.

Attachments: slo-proposal.pdf, perf-plan.xlsx

Best,

Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 09 Feb 2026 10:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Performance SLOs & Autoscale: FastPay discovery follow-up

Internal note — looping Vivek in to track an ask: Samir confirmed p95 <= 450ms and warm-pool target of 500 pre-warmed slots with burst to 2000 within ~60s. They are strict on a 3s queuing tolerance for non-priority traffic and sub-200ms for priority first-token.

Action items for us:
- Marissa: please include two costed options in the Monday deliverable (Dedicated reservation sized for 400-500 steady concurrency vs Hosted+Burst with 500 warm-pool + burst credits).
- Vivek: please prepare a short ops checklist for the perf run (GPU types, warm-pool pre-warm procedure, KV cache priming steps, monitoring hooks).
- I'll draft a short note for Operations/Capacity planning to ensure we can support pre-warm schedules during their forecasted peak windows.

Thanks,
Rafael
